content:
Apple has recently raised prices on most of its products, but the iPhone and other items are expected to see further price hikes next month.

The iPhone is expected to get more expensive with the iPhone 18 lineup, and the Apple Watch and AirPods could also be affected

Earlier this summer, Apple had already raised prices on several products.

Mac, iPad, Apple TV, HomePod, and Vision Pro all went up in price at the same time.

CEO Tim Cook had previewed the price hikes in advance, but seeing so many products increase in price all at once is still shocking.

In that round of increases, the only flagship products unaffected were:

  • iPhone
  • Apple Watch
  • AirPods

At the time, Apple hinted that more price hikes were coming, and analysts believed the few products that had been spared would soon see increases as well.

It is now widely expected that the iPhone will get more expensive at the September iPhone 18 event.

According to rumors, the iPhone 18 Pro is expected to start at $1,299 to $1,399, while the iPhone 17 Pro was priced at $1,099.

Apple typically lowers the price of older models when introducing new iPhones, but this year the older models are expected to either hold their price or see slight increases.

Both the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 could get more expensive, as the current AI-driven memory crisis also affects component costs for watches.

Finally, AirPods may also see a price hike. The likelihood is lower than for the iPhone and Apple Watch, since rising memory and storage chip costs should have a minimal impact on AirPods.

However, if Apple plans to raise prices across its entire lineup, including AirPods, that will be revealed at the September event.

What price changes do you expect from Apple? Let us know in the comments.
